newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy ready to do more on EMU deficit goal-Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italy ready to do more on EMU deficit goal-Ciampi.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Sunday that Italy was ready to take further steps to meet the goal of the three percent ratio between budget deficit and GDP required to join a European single currency.
"Certainly, reaching the objective of a three percent ratio between public administration deficit and gross domestic product this year is an arduous task," he told a foreign exchange conference.
"We know this and for that reason we are working with determination, ready for further measures."
He did not spell out what those measures could be.

"Italy is already more credible today than yesterday. It has decisively beaten inflation. It has earned a strong fall of interest rates in the market and its currency is maintaining itself without problems at its central parity," he said.
Ciampi said those achievements meant that Italy was respecting three parameters of the Maastricht treaty.
"It knows it is in a condition to bring strength to the euro not weakness," Ciampi said. The euro is due for launch in 1999.
Ciampi said that the conditions contained in a European stability pact on limiting budget deficit levels should be "no cause for alarm".
"The Italian economy is capable of returning to developing growth rates closer to its productive potential, with healthy state accounts, stable prices like in the 1950s," he said.
"The reduction in interest rates and the need in 1998 for a lower primary surplus will create easier conditions...which will spread from the public sector to the entire economy," Ciampi added.
